160010201.text: Hey, Durin! Any more clues for us? We're all set for the next chapter!

160010203.text: Yeah, I was just about to come find you... Let's see what it says.

160010204.text: Now sprout to life the story's seeds, stirred by windborne melodies.

160010205.text: Then on that breeze the music leaves, fading into distant memories.

160010206.text: Seek the place where wind and tale entwine, and once there, make three riddles into verse, and three melodies into song.

160010207.text: For in poetry and song will this story start to blossom.

160010209.text: C'mon, another riddle? All that talk about wind and melodies... Ugh, what do you think the answer could be?

160010210.text: Wind, melodies, Mondstadt... Are you thinking what I'm thinking?

160010213.text: Wind, music, poetry... Tone-Deaf Bard's gotta know the answer!

160010216.text: Albedo introduced us when I first arrived in Mondstadt. I mean, someone like me was bound to catch his eye sooner or later.

160010217.text: It's better that it's out in the open, anyway! Now, how should we track him down?

160010218.text: I'm pretty sure he's already "caught wind" of what's going on here. Why don't we just... see where the wind takes us?

160010219.text: Ah, right! He definitely makes it easy to forget he's a real god sometimes...

subQuests.subQuestName: Follow the guidance to find Venti

160010301.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... What a sight for sore eyes! Ah, and the little dragon from the fairytale world!

160010302.text: I heard your voices calling out to me on the wind. Something about... needing help with a riddle?

160010303.text: Sorry to disturb you, Lord Barbatos...

160010304.text: Hah, disturb me? Not at all! To tell you the truth, I'm just as curious about this riddle as you are. Let me take a look.

160010306.text: What is it? Did you figure out the answer?

160010307.text: Three riddles and three melodies... Hehe, that sure takes me back. The answer you seek lies hidden in memory.

160010308.text: Looks like running to Tone-Deaf Bard was the right call, after all!

160010309.text: Long ago, those mages came to Mondstadt, seeking to test their strength against mine.

160010310.text: But I replied, "Let us make music, not war, and resolve our conflicts through song."

160010311.text: So I strummed my lyre and sang them this verse:

160010312.text: "O wind, O wind, welcome now my guests."

160010313.text: "Pass through verdant leaves unseen, where shape your formless self may take, and offer up a graceful scene, a fleeting gift for welcome's sake."

160010314.text: "Leap at the edge of a sea of clouds, where land meets sky, and sky meets ground, there frighten off the noisy crowds, and bring my guests a calm profound."

160010315.text: "Fly beneath the stars up high, where mortal noise is swept aside, that my dear guests, with starry eyes, may share the dreams they hold inside."

160010316.text: "Now go to where I vowed to keep, a quiet spot for them to sleep."

160010317.text: "No clash, no contest bars the way, just tea and mirth to fill the day."

160010318.text: There you have it — the three melodies. As for the answers to those three riddles, I trust you can guess them by now?

160010319.text: The woods, the edge of a cliff, and... the sky?

160010320.text: Correct! Funnily enough, your mother was also the first to solve it, all that time ago.

160010321.text: Heh, there must be some kind of special rapport between those who write stories and those who sing them.

160010322.text: The woods, a cliff, and the sky... Ohhhh, so that's where it is!

160010323.text: I suppose the spot that answer points to is where you're headed next.

160010324.text: You should know, after solving my riddle, the mages even accepted my proposal, and made that location their official meeting spot.

160010325.text: And going by what your book is suggesting, once you've found it, you might wanna try playing the melody I just shared with you.

160010326.text: Guess you can be pretty reliable when it counts, huh, great Anemo Archon.

160010327.text: Thanks for the help, Lord Barbatos. Um...

160010328.text: Still got questions for me, huh?

160010329.text: Yeah, um... You must have read countless tales in your time, being a wandering bard and all. In your experience, why might an author consider a story "unfinished"?

160010330.text: Unfinished? Hm, well, I guess if there's something left to accomplish in the story, or um... Oh! If the last line goes: "To be continued..."

160010332.text: Well, your helpfulness lasted for, like, one second...

160010333.text: In all seriousness, I would think, the answer to that question lies in your mother's story itself. It's not my place to pry any further.

160010334.text: Hm... Alright then, we should get going.

subQuests.subQuestName: Head to the mages' meeting spot

160010401.text: Okay, we're here! Now, we just need to play the three melodies, and we should be able to gather the memories for the next chapter, right?

160010402.text: A musical performance, huh... Out of all the things Miss Lisa has taught me, that's the one I'm worst at...

subQuests.subQuestName: Enter the world within the book

160011001.text: I wonder when their next meeting will be...

subQuests.subQuestName: Learn the story from the narrator

160010507.text: So, we're back in the story world, huh...

160010508.text: As if from nowhere, new guests appeared at the witches' table. Perhaps they too had come to celebrate the dragon-child's birthday.

160010509.text: Yet while everyone else was busy thinking about what kind of gift to offer, these three seemed to have come... empty-handed.

160010510.text: ...Hardly the recipe for a warm welcome to a birthday party, now is it?

160010512.text: Hey, what's this all about? We only just found out this was a party!

160010513.text: While the guests voiced their complaints and grievances, perhaps they should have been wondering what kind of gift to give instead...

160010514.text: So, we need to bring a gift to advance the story... But where are we supposed to get something like that!?

160010515.text: Perhaps it would be a good idea to... have a look around.

160010516.text: Why didn't you just say so!?

160011101.text: (A toy sword. Perfect for a little warrior in the making.)

160010601.text: Hey, could we use these as gifts, maybe?

160010602.text: At last, the guests found something to give the dragon child.

160010603.text: Guess that's a yes, then... Hmm, which one should we go for?

160010604.text: Still, the guests wondered, what kind of gift might the little dragon really want?

160010605.text: Should they put a warrior's sword in his hand and send him out on an unstoppable quest to save the world?

160010606.text: Or perhaps a wandering hero's slingshot, and the promise of a life of endless, uncharted adventure?

160010607.text: Or maybe even a scholar's tome and the chance to take on all the world's unsolved mysteries?

160010608.text: Okay, wow, that's a lot of pressure all of a sudden...

160010610.text: Oh yeah! Technically, we're actually picking a gift for you! So... which one would you prefer?

160010611.text: You want... me to choose? Wow, this feels... kinda special.

160010613.text: For as long as I can remember, I've spent most of my time living in the stories my mother created.

160010614.text: I always thought my mother had everything written out for me already — just like the toy figures in Constellation Metropole. What I wanted to do with my own future... Huh, that's something I've never really thought about.

160010615.text: What did I want back then...? Ah... This is the first time I've ever asked myself that question.

160010616.text: Sounds like this is the perfect opportunity to answer it, then!

160010617.text: It's been a while since you left Simulanka. And, after everything that's happened, it might be about time to start thinking about your future.

160010618.text: Hm... Then let me give it some thought.

160011402.text: In the end, the guests settled on... the warrior's sword.

160011403.text: So your dream is to become a warrior?

160011404.text: I just... really want to be able to keep people safe.

160011405.text: If my time in Nod-Krai taught me anything, it's that a lot of problems in this world can only be settled by strength of arms.

160011406.text: As long as I can help people, that's enough for me.

160011407.text: You're doing a great job already.

160011408.text: Really? But... I don't think it's enough...

subQuests.subQuestName: Attend the birthday celebration with the gift

160010801.text: Alright, they should let us in now that we've got a gift, right?

160010802.text: Hello there. Brought a gift this time.

160010803.text: The newly arrived guest presented his gift, wishing the little dragon a future as an indomitable warrior.

160010804.text: The newly arrived guest presented his gift, wishing the little dragon a future as a wandering hero, free and unburdened.

160010805.text: The newly arrived guest presented his gift, wishing the little dragon a future as a wise and accomplished scholar.

160010806.text: Accepting the guest's blessing, the story-witch invited him and his friends to take their place around the table.

160010807.text: Finally, she could introduce them all to her dragon-child, telling all in attendance about the moment of his hatching, and of course, the name he'd been given...

160010808.text: It was then that the seer-witch, diviner of the stars, withdrew her gaze from the heavens and turned a sorrowful glance upon the little dragon.

160010809.text: You gave him the same name as that evil dragon?

160010810.text: That's right. But the life I intend for him shall be very different.

160010811.text: What folly, to love so blindly — for as you must know, a name is the mirror of destiny itself. He who bears an evil dragon's name must also inherit the fate of its previous owner.

160010814.text: The witches at the table fell silent, for they knew the seer-witch's words had never once proven wrong.

160010815.text: Yet just as clearly, they recognized the story-witch's resolve, for there is scarce a force in this world more fearsome than a mother's love.

160010816.text: At last, the merry-witch stepped forward, dispelling the uneasy silence.

160010817.text: So be it — then we'll all lend a hand. Together, we shall rewrite this child's fate!

160010818.text: You mean to defy one of the fundamental rules of this world?

160010819.text: I refuse to be shackled by such "rules." Besides, this is a witches' gathering, is it not? What could be more fitting a subject for this occasion than to defy them?

160010820.text: Oh? Sounds like an interesting experiment...

160010821.text: I suppose, were we to succeed in this endeavor, we might bring a touch of wonder to this otherwise dreary sky of stars...

160010822.text: The merry-witch finally talked them all round, just like she had done many times before.

160010823.text: Warm and strong as the sun she was — so much so, in fact, that those who her light shined down upon had no choice but to bask in it.

160010824.text: And so the witches readied their gifts, three marvels of the cosmos.

160010825.text: For this child, I shall decipher the ravings of the heavens and lay bare before him the trickery of fate.

160010826.text: For this child, I shall leave a formula powerful enough to unravel the very origins of this world, that he may seek another solution for the conundrum of his life.

160010827.text: For this child, I shall call upon wondrous magic to make possible his impossible wish.

160010828.text: All the story-witch had was the pen in her hand, yet with the love that flowed from it, she resolved to bring forth a marvel of her own.

160010829.text: For this child, I shall leave behind the last story I will ever write, and with it, a path to an ending yet untold.

160010830.text: With the witches' blessings given and received, the little dragon's fate at last began to turn.

160010901.text: Yep... Looks like we've completed this chapter, too.

160010902.text: Those witches in the story were the mages of the Hexenzirkel, right? They sure seemed to care a lot about you, Durin!

160010903.text: But, uh... Paimon kinda had trouble following their conversation. Just a bunch of mystery, as usual...

160010905.text: Ohhh, is that what you're worried about? But... didn't we already take care of that?

160010908.text: Ahh... The mages must have had a hand in that too.

160010909.text: Also, I was just thinking... Which part of the story are we even meant to be "completing"?

160010912.text: It feels less like we're filling in the gaps, and more like we're adding something new altogether...

160010913.text: But, we used the ink, right? And the book hasn't given us any more clues, so that must mean our task is complete — at least for now.

160010914.text: Yeah, I guess we're doing something right...

subQuests.subQuestName: Discuss your experience within the story with Durin

160010702.text: What the guests saw before them was none other than the witch's pen, the source of countless moving tales.

160010703.text: So this is M's pen? The one she used to write the story of Simulanka? You must know it well, Durin...

160010704.text: Honestly, the thing I remember most is how often I woke up to the sound of it scribbling away...

160010705.text: In the years before my mother passed away, she'd often sit at her desk writing late into the night. Almost like... like she was in a race against time to get something completed.

160010706.text: Sounds like a tough line of work...

160010707.text: Anyway, it belonged to my mother, so we shouldn't mess with it. Let's go see what else there is.

160011201.text: (A little slingshot. Just the thing for a wandering hero-to-be.)

160011301.text: (A tome. The ideal gift for a budding scholar.)

160011502.text: In the end, the guests settled on... the wandering hero's slingshot.

160011503.text: A wandering hero... So you're an explorer, just like us!

160011504.text: I guess you inspired me, hehe.

160011505.text: During our journey from Mondstadt to Nod-Krai, we passed through many places and encountered all sorts of different people.

160011506.text: But despite the immense distances between them, there was always one topic that kept cropping up — your accomplishments.

160011507.text: Hehe... Well, we are world-renowned adventurers, after all!

160011508.text: Come to think of it... Isn't a wandering hero basically the same thing as an adventurer?

160011509.text: I've always thought of adventurers as people who chase after stories, and in doing so, they also leave behind many of their own.

160011510.text: I'd like to become someone like that too.

160011602.text: In the end, the guests settled on... the scholar's tome.

160011603.text: So you're the scholarly type, huh?

160011604.text: I just feel like... I should learn more about the way the world works.

160011606.text: Um... I'll give you an example. Did you know that in Mondstadt, using fire to catch fish is a punishable offense?

160011607.text: I'm guessing... Klee took you fish blasting?

160011608.text: I thought she was just teaching me regular hunting techniques. It was only after Master Jean caught me and sent me to solitary confinement that I realized I'd misread the situation...

160011609.text: So much of what's considered common knowledge in your world just wasn't in Simulanka. So, I have to learn, or I'll keep causing trouble for everyone else.

160011610.text: Uh... Paimon's not sure that counts as "common" knowledge...

160011701.text: Hey, is that... the other Durin?

160011704.text: Nope, no reaction... Seriously, did he doze off at his own birthday party!?

160011705.text: Brought to life by the witch's magic ink, the dragon-child played with animated glee each time the tip of her pen danced across the page.

160011706.text: Yet she could not spend all her time writing. For the upcoming witches' gathering, she had no choice but to set down her pen.

160011707.text: But before doing so, she wrote one last line: "So did the child drift off into blissful slumber."

160011711.text: Strange, I don't remember ever being at any of the mages' gatherings. When exactly was this birthday party supposed to have happened...?

160011712.text: No wonder you don't remember — from the looks of it, you were probably fast asleep at the time!

160019903.text: The witches went on chatting away, ignoring the empty-handed guests.

160019904.text: The guests hesitated, and not without good reason. Given how much this gift would mean to the little dragon, a bit of careful thought could go a long way...

160019905.text: No mark had been left on the page ahead. The group found themselves unable to move forward...

160019906.text: For in poetry and song will this story start to blossom.

160019907.text: The witches readied their gifts, three marvels of the cosmos.
